text:
RECORD CORRECTION, and it is a THIRD ghost on this one bead.

An earlier note here says: "proposal C -- the cell-trace function -- DEPENDS on B, so C needs no
separate ruling until B lands. NO ACTION REQUIRED from the chief beyond the item 1 ruling." That was
mine and IT IS NOW FALSE IN BOTH HALVES. C did not depend on B in the way I assumed, and C has just
received a full chief ruling. Superseded by the decision note above it.

So this bead has carried three ghosts simultaneously:
  1. a precondition naming a state that will never occur (Semantic joining MayBeMissing)
  2. a claim that C depends on B
  3. a claim that no chief action was required
All three were written by people acting in good faith on what was true at the time, and all three
would have kept a reader from touching ready work.

PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2. It was P3 partly BECAUSE it read as blocked, which is the cost of ghost
records made concrete: a phantom blocker does not merely sit there, it depresses the priority of the
thing it blocks, and the priority outlives the phantom. C is approved, unblocked, and its design is
settled.

P2 IS NOT AN INSTRUCTION TO START NOW. My sequencing in the ruling stands: the eligible-set carrier
touches CostBreakdown, so it waits for the semantic candidate and 30fed2f to land. The function half
can start whenever m1 has capacity.
